Xbox’s CEO Spends a Few Hours a Month Answering Your Support Tickets

The detail comes from a WSJ profile that also paints a blunt picture of Xbox's finances.

Ahmed Shayan 19 hours ago
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:22
Instaread

Story Highlights

  • Asha Sharma personally works through Xbox player support tickets a few hours every month.
  • The detail comes from a new Wall Street Journal profile of the Xbox CEO.
  • She’s reportedly learned firsthand how messy fixing one player’s problem can get.

If you’ve filed an Xbox support ticket since February, there’s a small chance the CEO read it. A new Wall Street Journal profile of Asha Sharma reports that she sets aside a few hours each month to work through player support requests herself, and that the experience has shown her how complicated resolving a single player’s issue can actually be.

Sharma came into the job in February 2026 with no prior games industry experience, replacing Phil Spencer after 12 years, so going straight to the complaints is one way to close that gap fast.

Asha On Why She Took On The Responsibility Of Xbox CEO

The profile paints her as blunt and demanding. On why she took the job despite having no games industry background, Sharma told the Journal it came down to a simple test:

“It wasn’t, ‘Do I want to do this?’ but, ‘Do I believe the theory of the case that I can add unique value?'”

She’s applied the same directness internally, telling a recent town hall that companies need to get better at sharing hard news, a philosophy she’s condensed into a personal mantra: clarity is kindness. Stan Chudnovsky, who managed her at Meta, described her separately as intense and expecting the same work ethic from people around her.

That framing tracks with her first months in charge, which have included thousands of layoffs, cancelled projects, and studios like Double Fine and Compulsion Games being spun back out as independent companies, alongside changes players actually liked, like scrapping the unpopular Xbox AI assistant and making disc owners’ digital copies easier to access.

Whether a few hours of ticket triage moves the needle against all that is another question. The WSJ also reports Xbox revenue is declining with profit margins still low, and Sharma is chasing double-digit margins this fiscal year. Reading support tickets is a better sample than a slide deck, but it doesn’t fix a platform on its own.
